findings.evidence: "Station staff can also help with the same request in person." appears verbatim at the end of both paragraphs.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate sentence from one paragraph, or rewrite each occurrence so it explains what in person help actually covers for that specific request.
findings.location: Section "Station updates", first two paragraphs (the paragraph after the h2 "Station updates", and the one following it)
findings.violation: The sentence is repeated almost word for word across two consecutive paragraphs that describe two different requests (reviewing the schedule, and reporting a service issue), which makes the section read as templated filler rather than distinct information.

findings.evidence: alt text "Crews repainting the accessible parking spaces near the station entrance."
findings.fix: Add a sentence in the section that ties the photo to the parking work shown, or move the image into a section that actually discusses accessible parking.
findings.location: Section "Station updates", the photo below the second paragraph
findings.violation: The image shows parking lot repainting, but neither paragraph in this section mentions parking, painting, or the station entrance, so the photo has no visible connection to the text around it.

findings.evidence: table rows read "North / On time" and "South / On time" with no caption, title, or as of date anywhere near the table.
findings.fix: Add a caption or heading directly above the table stating what it shows and as of when, for example "Zone status as of today's date".
findings.location: Section "Schedule changes", the two column table listing Zone and Status
findings.violation: A reader arriving at the table without reading the surrounding paragraph in full has no way to tell what the table is reporting or how current the status is.

findings.evidence: "Route adjustments take effect on the posted effective date."
findings.fix: State the specific effective date directly, or turn "posted effective date" into a link that goes to where it is published.
findings.location: Section "Fare adjustments", the shaded box right after the second paragraph (the one styled as a promo banner)
findings.violation: The sentence refers to "the posted effective date" without ever stating what that date is or linking to where it is posted, so the sentence conveys no actual information to the reader.

findings.evidence: a trash can icon labeled "Delete item" with no visible text nearby explaining what item it refers to
findings.fix: Remove the control if it is left over from another template, or add visible text stating what it deletes immediately before it.
findings.location: Section "Fare adjustments", the small icon control between the status card and the step list
findings.violation: A delete control sits in the middle of fare adjustment content with nothing before or after it saying what will be deleted, so its purpose is unclear no matter how the page is read.

findings.evidence: the three step labels describe a plan purchase and checkout flow
findings.fix: Remove the step block if it does not belong on this page, or replace its labels with steps that actually describe the fare adjustment process the surrounding text is about.
findings.location: Section "Fare adjustments", the three step block ("Choose a plan", "Enter payment details", "Confirm your order")
findings.violation: Nothing else on this page is a purchase or checkout process; the section is about fare adjustments and route status, so these steps do not match the content around them and appear to belong to a different page.

findings.evidence: link text "read the accessibility improvements list"
findings.fix: Change the link text to match its destination and the surrounding sentence, for example "read the full list of upcoming fare adjustments."
findings.location: Section "Fare adjustments", the sentence just before the form ("For the full list of upcoming adjustments...")
findings.violation: The sentence and section are about fare adjustments, but the link text describes an "accessibility improvements list," so the link's own wording does not match what it points to.

findings.evidence: label reads "Phone number (required)" on a field with no required marking enforced on the input itself
findings.fix: Make the phone input actually required so the form's behavior matches what its label states.
findings.location: The form at the end of the "Fare adjustments" section, phone number field
findings.violation: The label promises the field is required, but nothing on the input enforces that, so a visitor can submit the form with the phone number left blank despite what the label says.

findings.evidence: the promo field is marked invalid, and the text "Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only" sits directly under it
findings.fix: Associate the error message with the promo input so it is announced when the field receives focus, for example by referencing the message's id from the input.
findings.location: The form, promo code field and the message below it
findings.violation: The error message is only connected to the field visually; nothing in the markup ties the message to the field, so a screen reader user focused on the field will not hear why it is marked invalid.

findings.evidence: label reads "Email address" with no "(required)" marker, unlike the phone field right below it
findings.fix: State each field's required or optional status consistently in every label, not only on the phone field.
findings.violation: The phone field states it is required but the email field gives no indication either way, so a user filling out the form cannot tell which fields are mandatory.
